question: For a horizontal curve radius of 500 feet, what approximate delineator spacing does Table 3G-1 show?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a curve radius of 500 feet, Table 3G-1 shows an approximate delineator spacing (S) of 65 feet on the curve. The MUTCD recommends that this table's spacing be used, adjusted so several delineators are always simultaneously visible; the tabulated values were rounded to the nearest 5 feet from the formula S=3√(R-50). Guidance (recommended): - "The spacing of delineators should be adjusted on approaches to and throughout horizontal curves so that several delineators are always simultaneously visible to the road user. The approximate spacing shown in Table 3G-1 should be used." - Per the table notes: spacing for specific radii may be interpolated, the minimum spacing should be 20 feet, and the spacing on curves should not exceed 300 feet. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 3G-1, in which the row for a 500-foot radius lists an approximate spacing of 65 feet; [Image 2] shows the same table in the context of page 621, confirming the 500 feet / 65 feet pairing and the notes on interpolation, minimum spacing, and the formula S=3√(R-50). Citations: - Table 3G-1 (p.621) - Section 3G.04 Support §13 (p.622) - Section 3G.04 Guidance §10 (p.620)
